findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate the audit-log datetime field
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering by `-datetime`, but this paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `item.datetime`. Django model datetimes are `datetime` objects, so even the first optimized request reaches `build_cursor` and raises `TypeError` rather than returning a page. It also lacks the datetime cursor conversion implemented by `DateTimePaginator`, so cursor-following requests would compare the datetime column to a raw integer. The optimized paginator must support datetime keys (for example, subclass/use `DateTimePaginator` behavior) before it can be used by this endpoint.

findings.title: Changing live Redis set keys to sorted sets is not rollout-compatible
findings.body: Existing buffered segments are Redis Sets (`SADD`/`SSCAN`), while this change writes the identical `span-buf:s:{...}` keys with `ZADD` and the Lua script reads/merges them with sorted-set commands. During a rolling deployment, any segment created by an old worker and still within its TTL will cause `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, or `ZUNIONSTORE` to fail with Redis `WRONGTYPE`; the processing batch then fails and spans cannot be buffered. Use versioned keys or a migration/compatibility path until all old keys have expired.

findings.title: Reducing redirect traversal can split deep traces into incorrect segments
findings.body: The redirect-chain traversal limit was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 with no fallback or indication that the chain was truncated. For a trace whose spans arrive in an order that creates more than 1,000 redirects, the script stops before reaching the actual segment key, writes the new span under an intermediate key, and records a redirect to that intermediate key. Those buffers can flush separately, producing incomplete/incorrect segments. Retain the prior bound or explicitly handle a truncated traversal so the span is joined to the true root.
